findings.issue: The table only lists rejections that come from reject() plus the missing module. CTG5 can produce other new failures that reach clients through the legacy StynxErrorFilter shape. Database.tx({requireActor:true}) throws TransactionIdentityMismatchError and ActorContextMissingError on a live role/tenant/actor mismatch; advanced spec:482 (wrong-role pool) reaches this and asserts only >=400. There are also raw Errors: non-HTTP context (:299), a scope callback that throws (:322), an invalid status (:367), persistStatus returning a non-boolean (:376), a non-JSON committed body (:193), and audit sink or store failures. As written, the claim that every new rejection uses the canonical envelope is false. The shape of these responses stays undecided.
findings.repair: Add a complete classification row for each of these paths. Either (a) map it to a canonical code after rollback, e.g. COMMAND:FORBIDDEN:transaction-identity-mismatch 403, COMMAND:FORBIDDEN:actor-missing 403, COMMAND:CONFIGURATION:scope-callback-failed / status-policy-invalid / response-not-json 500, or (b) state explicitly that it is an internal error delegated to the global StynxErrorFilter, outside option A, and record the real runtime shape in errors.json. Pin each choice with a sensor. For advanced spec:482, assert the exact status and body.

findings.issue: Bootstrap validation of mismatchCode breaks shared fixtures. The ProvenanceController route with mismatchCode:'' and the advanced route with 'SCOPED_COMMAND_MISMATCH' fail the schema pattern, so app.init() will refuse and take down both entire suites. The proposal also keeps the COMMAND_MISMATCH_CODE_INVALID 500 row in the table while saying bootstrap validation replaces the late rejection. mismatchCode is a static string, so that row is unreachable.
findings.repair: Remove the COMMAND:CONFIGURATION:mismatch-code-invalid row, or mark it explicitly unreachable and cover it only by a unit test of the centralized constructor. The Inspector moves /invalid-option into its own bootstrap-refusal test (app.init rejects with a named error, before listen) and replaces 'SCOPED_COMMAND_MISMATCH' with a conforming custom code such as 'SCOPED:CONFLICT:command-mismatch'. It keeps the assertion that the configured code is emitted, which is the UPS-TXN-03 configurability proof. The dispatch should record that this is a fixture migration, not a weakening.

findings.issue: The Inspector list leaves out the only 503 sensor. The no-module spec asserts only status >=400, and the proposal requires a real Nest sensor for the 503. It also leaves out if-match-http.spec.ts, which stacks RequireIfMatch and TransactionalCommand filters on the same method. The bootstrap check catchesCommitted() and the new rejection filter interact there. Today CommandModuleRequiredInterceptor throws a plain HttpException({code}) that CommittedCommandResponseFilter's @Catch does not match, so it falls through to the global filter.
findings.repair: Add both files to the Inspector lock. no-module: assert status 503 exactly and the complete envelope, X-Request-Id equal to body.requestId, and no code/context, both with and without StynxCoreModule (RequestContext absent), with the handler not called. if-match: assert that 412/428 keep the IFM envelope and 409 uses the CTG5 envelope on the combined route, in both decorator orders. If the method filter cannot be reached without the module provider (it currently registers as a controller-module injectable that depends only on HttpAdapterHost), the Engineer must return reference-gap.

findings.issue: Nine codes have no named sensor: MODULE_REQUIRED, MARKING_REQUIRED, CONTEXT_MISSING, ACTOR_OR_TENANT_MISSING, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, LOCK_TIMEOUT_INVALID, IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_INVALID, BODY_INVALID and CLAIMS_MISMATCH (grep finds none). Several existing assertions are weak: advanced:405 accepts any 4xx, advanced:482 accepts >=400, provenance:207 checks only the status. The instruction to assert the full body in every reachable branch does not say which branches are reachable. lockTimeoutMs and ttlMs are static options/metadata, yet they stay as per-request 500s instead of being validated at bootstrap like mismatchCode.
findings.repair: The Architect publishes a reachability matrix per row: reachable over HTTP gets an exact-body test; unreachable gets documentation plus a unit test of the constructor. Validate lockTimeoutMs (forRoot and route) and ttlMs (@Idempotent metadata) at bootstrap, with a refusal test, or justify keeping them at request time. Replace every >=400 and toMatchObject({code}) with toEqual of the full envelope.

findings.issue: retryable:false on IDEMPOTENCY:CONFLICT:in-progress contradicts the schema's retryable description. In-progress contention is transient: the same request with the same key, retried after the winner commits, gets a replay. false would tell clients such as the Angular interceptor and DETRAN not to retry. errors.json also uses the key retriable, while the schema uses retryable.
findings.repair: The Owner/Architect should decide explicitly. The recommendation is retryable:true for in-progress, optionally with Retry-After, and false for duplicate-key and for the 4xx/5xx configuration errors. Record both the wire field and the catalog key in errors.json, and have the Inspector assert the value exactly.

findings.issue: The triad misses or misassigns several documents. The README 409 prose is hand-written; scripts/generate-package-readmes.mjs renders only the dependency section, so 'pelo gerador oficial' does not update it. The fixed-group changeset does not mention the new envelope, the default code, or the pattern narrowing of mismatchCode, and no role is assigned to it. The errors.json description ('architectural target, not the literal runtime shape') and the duplicate-key row ('different request body') need to cover method and concrete path and the new runtime shape. The CTG5 contract text on fingerprint and on the Inspector proof still names IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS and {code, context}.
findings.repair: Assign the README prose and the changeset to a named role (Engineer, or Architect if treated as a contract) and put both in the lock list. The Architect amends every occurrence in the CTG5 contract, including sections 'Fingerprint' and 'Inspector proof', plus the errors.json description and the duplicate-key and in-progress rows with runtimeBody. Record the DETRAN consumer impact (code→errorCode, pattern-validated mismatchCode) in the migration note and the C-0002 §7 ledger.

findings.issue: The API baseline rebind is practically certain, not conditional. Resolving requestId the way IfMatchExceptionFilter does requires @Optional() RequestContext in the exported CommittedCommandResponseFilter constructor, which changes transactional-command.d.ts and its declarationHash. A new exported rejection type or code constants would do the same. The locks also need ordering. The Architect's pre-Inspector docs commit, the trace rebind after the Inspector commit (check:trace goes red until then), and the baselines rebind after the Engineer commit are three separate Architect commits. The angular spec is a CTG7 artifact, so editing it under CTG5 crosses CTG locks.
findings.repair: State the order in the plan: Architect docs → Inspector tests (red) → Architect trace.json rebind → Engineer src → Architect api:baselines:write after confirming the d.ts diff, all authored as DEVAI Architect. Keep CommandRejectionResponse unexported. Record in the ledger that the CTG7 angular spec is edited under CTG5 authority, with assertions only strengthened. Touch none of the three package.json files, to avoid the local-rc-blocker freeze.

findings.issue: The shared filter must split its branches. For CommandRejectionResponse it must resolve requestId (context → normalized response header → normalized request header → UUIDv7) and set X-Request-Id. For CommittedCommandResponse it must not touch the body or rewrite the persisted bytes, including the chosen 502 and CommittedCommandError(422). The singleton filter must not cache the ID. The proposal does not require proof for concurrency or for an invalid inbound header without core.
findings.repair: Required evidence: two concurrent 409 losers each have body.requestId equal to their own X-Request-Id, and the two differ. With no core and X-Request-Id 'not-a-uuid', the response gets a fresh UUIDv7 and the raw value is never echoed. After the envelope change, the 502 replay and CommittedCommandError(422) stay byte-identical (http.spec:242-310, filters:224). The legacy 422 IDEMPOTENT_KEY_REUSE_DIFFERENT_BODY and the global StynxErrorFilter keep their sensors unchanged.

summary: This is a conditional, pre-dispatch technical review. It does not replace the Owner approval that INV-ERROR-001.change_policy requires, and that approval is still pending. Option A is the right direction. It keeps UPS-TXN-03 satisfied, because the 409 stays configurable and is constrained to the law pattern. It does not touch law/, the 422 legacy response, or the bodies chosen by consumers. It follows the If-Match precedent (IfMatchExceptionFilter), which already emits the law envelope with the same requestId resolution order. It is not yet complete enough for dispatch. (1) 'Todas as rejeições' is not true: CTG5 errors outside reject() are unclassified. These are requireActor/TransactionIdentityMismatchError, which the wrong-role test reaches, and raw Errors from the scope, persistStatus, status and non-JSON body paths. (2) Bootstrap validation of mismatchCode knocks down the provenance and advanced fixtures ('' and 'SCOPED_COMMAND_MISMATCH'). It also contradicts keeping the 500 mismatch-code-invalid row. (3) The only 503 sensor (transactional-command-no-module, which asserts >=400) and if-match-http.spec.ts are missing from the Inspector list. Today the 503 is not even caught by the CTG5 filter. (4) Nine codes have no named sensor, and lockTimeoutMs/ttlMs could be validated at bootstrap. (5) retryable:false on in-progress contradicts the schema's semantics. (6) README prose, the changeset, errors.json and contract text are missing or misassigned. (7) The API baseline rebind is practically certain (the filter constructor changes), and the three Architect commits need explicit ordering, plus the cross-CTG7 lock on the angular spec. Minimum evidence for a delivery PASS, all at the same HEAD: a red-then-green log of the focused CTG5 tests against real PostgreSQL as stynx_app with two tenants. Every reachable rejection asserted with toEqual of the full envelope, with no code/context, body.requestId equal to X-Request-Id, and durable key/audit/domain state unchanged. Bootstrap refusal tests for invalid mismatchCode (forRoot and route) and a sensor comparing the runtime pattern with the schema pattern. The 503 without the module, with and without core. A concurrent 409 race with distinct requestIds. Rollback negatives, the 502 replay and CommittedCommandError(422) byte-identical. The legacy 422 and the global filter unchanged. check:rls-negative, check:rls-smoke, check:trace (after rebind), api:baselines (after rebind), backend lint and typecheck, package-readmes:check, DEVAI strict, and a recorded Owner receipt. Verdict: REVIEW. Fix findings 1–3 in the proposal before dispatch, and incorporate 4–8 into the Inspector and Architect prompts.
